nodes.title: Store the selection as a mode plus exceptions
nodes.why: Select all must cover files on pages that were never rendered. A mode of all with a set of unticked ids describes that selection without listing every id, and a deselection on page two is one more exception.
nodes.alternative: Keep a set of selected ids and add every matching id on select all.
nodes.tradeoff: A plain id set is simpler to read but grows with the export and forgets files the filter has not loaded yet; the mode stays the same size.

nodes.title: Derive the matching rows from the filter and the sort
nodes.why: The visible page is a slice of one derived list, so filtering, sorting and paging can never disagree with each other or with the selection.
nodes.alternative: Copy the filtered and sorted rows into state from an effect.
nodes.tradeoff: A copy in state renders once with stale rows and can drift; the memo recomputes only when the filter or the sort changes.

nodes.title: Decide selection by file id and availability
nodes.why: A row is selected because of its id, never its position, so a sort cannot move a tick to another file, and an unavailable file is never counted.
nodes.alternative: Track selected row indexes on the current page.
nodes.tradeoff: Indexes break on every sort, filter and page change; ids survive all three.

nodes.title: Derive the header state from counts
nodes.why: The header reflects every matching file, not the rendered rows, so it turns mixed as soon as one file on any page is unticked.
nodes.alternative: Check whether every rendered row is ticked.
nodes.tradeoff: Looking at the rendered rows reports all when only the current page is ticked.

nodes.title: Set the indeterminate property in an effect
nodes.why: The mixed look of a checkbox is a DOM property with no HTML attribute, so React cannot render it; an effect sets it after each change, and aria-checked="mixed" tells assistive technology the same thing.
nodes.alternative: Render a custom mixed icon instead of a native checkbox.
nodes.tradeoff: A custom control needs its own keyboard and screen reader behavior; the native checkbox keeps both.

nodes.title: Clear the selection when the filter changes
nodes.why: A selection made under one filter would otherwise download files the user can no longer see. Clearing it, and returning to page one, keeps the download honest.
nodes.alternative: Keep hidden selections and show how many are hidden by the filter.
nodes.tradeoff: Keeping them is friendlier for long sessions but needs a visible hidden count; clearing is simpler and has to be said out loud in the review.

nodes.title: Show an empty line and gate the download on the count
nodes.why: The download button reads the same count as the summary, so it is enabled exactly when something is selected, and a filter with no match shows an empty line instead of an empty table.
nodes.alternative: Enable the button and validate the selection on click.
nodes.tradeoff: A disabled button tells the user why nothing can happen before they try.
